title: Unramifiedness from ordinary fibres
statement: Let $h:Z\to B$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every point $s\in B$, let $Z_s=Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], where $\kappa(s)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. If each $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is a disjoint union of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite separable algebraic field extensions [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] of $\kappa(s)$, then $h$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq B$ containing $h(z)$. By the locally-of-finite-type hypothesis [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $h^{-1}(V)$ has an affine open cover by schemes $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a finitely generated $R$-algebra; let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a member of this cover containing $z$, so $h(U)\subseteq V$ and $R\to A$ is finitely generated. For every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, let $s\in V\subseteq B$ be the corresponding point; since $V$ is open, $\kappa(s)=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to B$ factors through $V$, so the fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] $U_s=U\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)=U\times_V\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. It is an open subscheme of $Z_s$ (the base change of the open immersion $U\hookrightarrow Z$, i.e. the preimage of $U$ under the projection $Z_s\to Z$). By the hypothesis and the existing field-fibre decomposition criterion [lem-trf-unramified-field-fibre-decomposition], $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is unramified; its restriction to the open $U_s$ is unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open], clause (2) with $V=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Thus for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the fibre morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is unramified.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02G8, part (2), proof; the fibre restriction uses Tag 02G6 and base change Tag 02GA

proof.text: For each $\mathfrak p$, apply the affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] to the unramified fibre $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ from step 1. It gives $\Omega_{(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$. Kähler differentials commute with this base change by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], so after identifying the fibre module with $(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))\otimes_A\Omega_{A/R}$, we obtain $\Omega_{A/R}\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak q)=0$ for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ over $\mathfrak p$. Because $A$ is finitely generated over $R$, the module $\Omega_{A/R}$ is generated by the differentials of a finite set of algebra generators (using the definition [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), hence is finite. Localize at $\mathfrak q$ and apply Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to the finite module $(\Omega_{A/R})_{\mathfrak q}$: its quotient by the maximal ideal is zero, so the localization is zero. Since this holds at every prime, $\Omega_{A/R}=0$. The affine criterion therefore gives that $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, and hence $h|_U$, is unramified.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 02G8, part (2), proof; Algebra, Lemmas Tags 00UW (unramified at a prime), 00RV (differential base change), and 00DV (Nakayama)

proof.text: The affine opens $U$ chosen in step 1 cover $Z$, and every restriction $h|_U$ is unramified by step 2. The affine-cover characterization in the definition of an unramified morphism [def-weil-unramified-morphism] (locally finite type together with finite-type affine charts having vanishing relative differentials, equivalently an open-immersion diagonal) therefore gives that $h$ itself is unramified.

lean.statement: theorem unramified_of_ordinary_fibre_coproduct_finite_separable {Z B : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ B) [LocallyOfFiniteType h] : (∀ s : B, ∃ (I : Type u) (L : I → Type u) (hfield : ∀ i, Field (L i)) (halg : ∀ i, Algebra (B.residueField s) (L i)), (∀ i, @Module.Finite (B.residueField s) (L i) inferInstance (hfield i).toCommRing.toRing.toAddCommGroup.toAddCommMonoid (halg i).toModule) ∧ (∀ i, @Algebra.IsSeparable (B.residueField s) (L i) inferInstance (hfield i).toCommRing.toRing (halg i)) ∧ ∃ e : h.fiber s ≅ ∐ (fun i : I ↦ Spec (CommRingCat.of (L i))), e.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun i : I ↦ (Spec.homEquiv (R := B.residueField s) (S := CommRingCat.of (L i))).symm (CommRingCat.ofHom (@algebraMap (B.residueField s) (L i) inferInstance (hfield i).toCommRing.toSemiring (halg i)))) = h.fiberToSpecResidueField s) → LocallyOfFiniteType h ∧ IsOpenImmersion (pullback.diagonal h)
